pr_title: [QUIC] Support for OpenSSL build of MsQuic on Windows (Attempt 2)
pr_body:
Closes #69978.

The problem with the original PR (#72262) was that in case that an incompatible MsQuic version was loaded, we didn't close the API Table handle before unloading the library. This led to us unloading the library while some code was still executing on a background MsQuic thread which crashed the process (this was way more probable on Release configurations than on Debug). This PR reintroduces the feature with appropriate changes.

issue_context.title: [QUIC] Support for OpenSSL build of MsQuic on Windows
issue_context.body:
Currently, we assume that on Windows, MsQuic always uses Schannel for TLS operations and on Linux it uses OpenSSL. This influences how we pass certificates to MsQuic

https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/a4223dc25e6c0ff7da1185f0559b40d0ae75d3da/src/libraries/System.Net.Quic/src/System/Net/Quic/Implementations/MsQuic/Interop/SafeMsQuicConfigurationHandle.cs#L183-L221

And also some certificate related flags: https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/a4223dc25e6c0ff7da1185f0559b40d0ae75d3da/src/libraries/System.Net.Quic/src/System/Net/Quic/Implementations/MsQuic/Interop/SafeMsQuicConfigurationHandle.cs#L55-L58

However, it is possible to build MsQuic with OpenSSL for Windows (e.g. to use on older Windows without TLS 1.3 support via Schannel). So we should instead make these decision based on the actual TLS backend being used. This information can be retrieved via recently added API: https://github.com/microsoft/msquic/pull/2762.

https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/72262 would be reverted in https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/72456, because it supposedly triggered strange native crashes on schannel-unsupported platforms, see https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/72429. We need to investigate before reintroducing the change.

review_comments: I guess we had the same issue before your change as well, we just never hit the right set of conditions for it to manifest and with your original change it happened on every Windows non-TLS1.3 machine.

Yes, we did not hit it before because the OS version check was before we opened the MsQuic library. I had to move the OS check later once we knew which TLS backend MsQuic is using.

We could have still hit the issue when opening an older MsQuic version on sufficiently new Windows OS
